$comment: Reachable (symbol-level) advisories that are knowingly accepted.
scripts/check-vuln.mjs runs govulncheck per module and fails on any
reachable advisory that is not listed here. Adding an entry is a security
decision that needs the compensating control and a review date, not a way to
make a red build go green.
`scope: reachable` means the module's own code calls the vulnerable symbol,
not merely that the module is in the build graph.
The gate refuses an entry that does not declare module, title, scope, impact,
compensatingControls, reviewed and revisitWhen, so an exception cannot be a

accepted.title: Server panic via missing authority or Host headers
accepted.affects: every module that runs a gRPC server
detail: The advisory was revised during the remediation. Its fix landed in
pre-release pseudo-version. v1.84.0 is the newest stable release and is
still reported as affected, so there is no stable version to move to.
Pulling an unreleased build into a financial production image is a worse
trade than the bounded availability risk below, so the dependency stays
on the latest stable and the exposure is reduced at the edges instead.
This entry replaced three advisories that the same upgrade did close:
GO-2026-6348 (heap exhaustion via HTTP/2 DATA frame fragmentation),
GO-2026-6061 (HTTP/2 transport) and, in golang.org/x/text, GO-2026-5970
(infinite loop on invalid input, reachable through the Kratos password
accepted.impact: availability only: no code execution and no data access
accepted.blastRadius: one gRPC server process exits and is restarted by its Deployment; the trace runs through grpc.Server.Serve, so the panic is in the transport and is not covered by the per-RPC recovery interceptor
compensatingControls: k8s/network-policies/arda-app grants ingress to gRPC port 9090 only from pods in the arda-app namespace, never from the Traefik edge controller or any other namespace
every gRPC-serving Deployment runs 3 replicas, so a single crash-loop is not an outage
the plaintext 9090 listener is cluster-internal; cross-service identity uses the mTLS listener, which fails closed when a client certificate is absent
Gatus asserts /health/ready on every service, so a crash-looping gRPC server raises an alert rather than sitting silent
pod memory and CPU limits are set, so the same class of memory-pressure bug is contained to one pod
accepted.revisitWhen: google.golang.org/grpc publishes a stable release containing commit 93e31b48545e; bump the dependency and delete this entry
